Estimate conditional treatment-effect scores for binary outcomes

Source: R/CATE_binary.R
catefitbinary.Rd

Fit binary-outcome CATE scores and estimate risk differences in nested subgroups. This is the binary-outcome interface used by catefit.

Usage

catefitbinary(
  data,
  outcome_model = NULL,
  outcome_method = NULL,
  benefit_method = NULL,
  ps.model,
  ps.method = "glm",
  minPS = 0.01,
  maxPS = 0.99,
  higher.y = TRUE,
  prop.cutoff = seq(0.5, 1, length = 6),
  seed = NULL,
  ps.control = list(),
  B = 3,
  Kfold = 5,
  tree.depth = 2,
  n.trees.boosting = 200,
  plot.gbmperf = FALSE,
  init.model = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing the variables in the outcome, treatment, and censoring models (if specified); a data frame with n rows (1 row per observation).

outcome_model

Outcome and score covariate formula; replaces cate.model.

outcome_method

Outcome-model methods paired with benefit_method; see catefit.

benefit_method

Score-construction methods; see catefit.

ps.model

A formula describing the treatment model (propensity-score model) to be fitted. The treatment must appear on the left-hand side. For binary outcomes, logical treatment values FALSE and TRUE are mapped to 0 and 1, respectively. Numeric 0/1 values or two distinct treatment labels are also accepted. If data are from a randomized controlled trial, specify ps.model = trt ~ 1 as an intercept-only model.

ps.method

A character value for the method to estimate the propensity score. Allowed values include one of: 'glm' for logistic regression with main effects only (default), or 'lasso' for a logistic regression with main effects and LASSO penalization on two-way interactions (added to the model if interactions are not specified in ps.model). Relevant only when ps.model has more than one variable.

minPS

A numerical value (in `[0, 1]`) below which estimated propensity scores should be truncated. Default is 0.01.

maxPS

A numerical value (in `(0, 1]`) above which estimated propensity scores should be truncated. Must be strictly greater than minPS. Default is 0.99.

higher.y

A logical value indicating whether higher (TRUE) or lower (FALSE) values of the outcome are more desirable. Default is TRUE.

prop.cutoff

A vector of numerical values (in `(0, 1]`) specifying percentiles of the estimated log CATE scores to define nested subgroups. Each element represents the cutoff to separate observations in nested subgroups (below vs above cutoff). The length of prop.cutoff is the number of nested subgroups. An equally-spaced sequence of proportions ending with 1 is recommended. Default is seq(0.5, 1, length = 6).

seed

An optional integer specifying an initial randomization seed for reproducibility. Default is NULL, corresponding to no seed.

ps.control

Named options for LASSO propensity-score interaction screening. Supported entry: solver = "C" (default) or solver = "R". Only affects screening when ps.method = "lasso"; the LASSO fit and interaction selection rule are unchanged. Kept separate from boosting's ... and other numerical controls.

B

A positive integer specifying the number of time cross-fitting is repeated in score.method = 'twoReg' and 'contrastReg'. Default is 3.

Kfold

A positive integer specifying the number of folds used in cross-fitting to partition the data in score.method = 'twoReg' and 'contrastReg'. Default is 5.

tree.depth

A positive integer specifying the depth of individual trees in boosting (usually 2-3). Used only if score.method = 'boosting' or if initial.predictor.method = 'boosting' with score.method = 'twoReg' or 'contrastReg'. Default is 2.

n.trees.boosting

A positive integer specifying the maximum number of trees in boosting (usually 100-1000). Used if score.method = 'boosting' or if initial.predictor.method = 'boosting' with score.method = 'twoReg' or 'contrastReg'. Default is 200.

plot.gbmperf

A logical value indicating whether to plot the performance measures in boosting. Used only if score.method = 'boosting' or if score.method = 'twoReg' or 'contrastReg' and initial.predictor.method = 'boosting'. Default is FALSE.

init.model

Optional formula for the initial logistic outcome models used by twoReg; NULL uses outcome_model.

...

Additional boosting arguments; see boosting-control.

Value

A catefit object containing treatment labels, fitted models, predicted risk-difference scores and nested subgroup risk differences for each requested method. Linear twoReg score coefficients are stored in coefficients.

Details

The legacy arguments score.method and cate.model are accepted through ...; see catefit.

See the Binary outcomes section of catefit for the score methods, their assumptions, and interpretation. Subgroup effects are estimated on the fitting data and do not provide independent validation.

Author

Thomas Debray tdebray@fromdatatowisdom.com

Examples

# \donttest{
dat <- simulate_binary(n = 400, seed = 2026)
fit <- catefitbinary(data = dat,
                     outcome_model = y ~ age + previous_treatment,
                     outcome_method = "logistic",
                     benefit_method = "t_learner",
                     ps.model = trt ~ age + previous_treatment,
                     seed = 2026)
# }
